subject: Private hosting feasibility — consolidated asks & architecture risks (Northbridge pilot)
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2026 09:23:00 -0700
Subject: Private hosting feasibility — initial consolidated asks (Northbridge pilot)

Team,

Following the call with Northbridge last week, I'm consolidating the asks into one place so we can align on architecture risks, staffing asks, and whether we need a formal exception lane for this pilot. High level context: Northbridge (healthcare payer) wants a 3-month pilot in their VPC with isolated data processing, dedicated KV cache persistence, and the ability to run our runtime on their on-prem GPU hosts for red-team validation. They want a security & evidence package (SOC 2+network diagrams) within 2 weeks to move to legal. Jordan pushed that this is a high-probability close and a reference if we can meet timelines.

Asks (what I need back by EOD Thu 9/23):
- Architecture: short summary of integration surface and any deal-blocking risks (networking, certs, KV persistence, model variant compatibility). Attach a single-slide diagram if possible.
- Ops staffing: estimated FTE-days for pilot setup, runbook creation, and on-call coverage for the 3-month pilot.
- Security: list of gaps to provide SOC2 evidence or compensating controls; note any escalation we should open with Security.
- Exceptions: confirm whether this requires a formal product/platform exception (yes/no) and what triggers it.

Attachments: pilot_scope_moa.pdf (summary from sales).

Thanks — I will collate and send a one-pager to Jordan/Cara for legal.

Hannah
Hannah Schmitt | Head, Product Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2026 11:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private hosting feasibility — initial consolidated asks (Northbridge pilot)

Hannah —

Quick tech summary (first-pass; will refine if we take this to engineering grooming):
- Integration surface: inbound TLS from Northbridge to a peered VPC private endpoint + mutual TLS for model requests. We will need a customer-managed NAT/egress control or an explicit egress allowlist; otherwise our telemetry/metrics pipeline will need to be routed via an approved aggregator.
- KV persistence: their ask for persistent KV across restarts on customer HW is doable but needs a light agent and a secure key wrapping flow (KMS/HSM handshake). That adds ~3–4 dev-days (agent + integration test).
- On-prem GPU runtime: our on-prem runtime can run but we haven't validated with their exact GPU SKU (old Ampere variant). Expect 5–7 engineering days for compatibility testing and a small kernel fallback patch if we hit instruction-set mismatches.
- Network diagram attached: pilot_network_diagram.png (high level).
- Deal-blockers: (1) audit log retention differences — we currently ship logs to our hosted observability; customer wants audit logs retained on-prem for 12 months (compensating control possible but must be approved). (2) Auto-update/rollback: our standard runtime auto-update must be disabled for isolated installs — operational risk for security team.

Ops staffing estimate (for pilot phase):
- Setup & runbook: 5 engineer-days (infra + solutions).
- Security artifact prep & evidence: 3 engineer-days + 1 SRE liaison (part-time).
- On-call rotations for 3-month pilot: 0.25 FTE (shared across oncall roster) — we can scope to a lightweight pager schedule.

Recommendation: open an exception ticket scoped to (a) audit log retention and (b) auto-update policy for the pilot. Security will need to sign off on compensating controls. If we can get a 2-week window for compatibility testing we can meet the legal ask.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer — Infrastructure Architect
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Cara Lopez <cara.lopez@northbridgehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Sep 2026 08:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private hosting feasibility — initial consolidated asks (Northbridge pilot)

Thanks team — Jordan here. Quick sales context: Northbridge has a program committee meeting on Oct 6th where they want a sign-off from Legal + Security to proceed to procurement. If we can't produce the requested evidence and a clear runbook plan by Oct 2nd they're unlikely to commit to the pilot timeline. They have asked us for a single consolidated artifact that shows architecture, controls, and drop-dead dates.

Two pragmatic asks from my side:
1) Can we compress Karthik's 5–7 days of compatibility validation to a 48–72 hour smoke test for the specific GPU SKU they provided? If so I can ask the customer to delay the wider validation until after initial pilot kickoff.
2) If we require an exception for audit log retention, can we estimate what the temporary compensating control looks like (e.g., encrypted push to a customer-controlled S3 with Hardened IAM for 90 days) and the engineering cost?

I can provide a partially-signed mutual NDA and push Legal to accept a staged evidence delivery. Also linking the HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.redwood/deal/NB-2026-1147. Cara — can you confirm whether Oct 6th is a hard date for your committee?

—Jordan
Jordan Blake | Senior Account Executive
From: Cara Lopez <cara.lopez@northbridgehealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Northbridge Health Legal <legal@northbridgehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 23 Sep 2026 10:32:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Private hosting feasibility — initial consolidated asks (Northbridge pilot)

Jordan/Hannah —

Oct 6th is the committee date; it's tight but possible. We can accept staged delivery for some items but Security will require either (a) SOC2 report + network diagram, or (b) a compensating controls plan with an explicit retention and access model. For the GPU validation: we can accept a 72-hour smoke test as a gating item for kickoff provided Redwood commits to full compatibility testing during the pilot and supplies a patch plan.

I'll upload the GPU SKU / environment details to the Drive link you shared and can sign a limited-scope NDA if that helps. Legal would prefer the evidence package by Oct 2nd to have time to review before committee.

Thanks — Cara
Cara Lopez | Director, Infrastructure Security
Northbridge Health

Subject: Re: Private hosting feasibility — initial consolidated asks (Northbridge pilot)

Team — thanks for the input. Summary & next steps (action owner):
- Karthik: run the 72-hour GPU smoke test (starting Mon 10/4) and produce a one-page compatibility note + risk severity. Attach network diagram and list of required certs. (action: Karthik; due: 10/7)
- Security/SRE liaison (Grace): prepare compensating-controls draft for audit log retention + auto-update disablement. Open exception ticket and tag Security. (action: Grace; due: 10/2)
- Ops (Monica): draft minimal runbook for pilot install, including rollback and monitoring playbook; include estimated on-call commitment. (action: Monica; due: 10/2)
- Jordan: continue to manage the customer expectations and obtain the limited-scope NDA. (action: Jordan; ongoing)

I've attached SOC2-questions.xlsx with a prioritized list of evidence items for Security to answer. I'm opening the exception ticket here: https://docs.redwood/ops/exception-ticket-4578 — please add comments there rather than replying-all to keep audits tidy.

If we can get the compatibility note + controls draft by Oct 2nd we can push a compliant package to Northbridge and aim for the Oct 6th committee. Thanks again — I will escalate to the Platform Product Council if we hit blockers.

Hannah
Hannah Schmitt | Head, Product Operations
Redwood Inference
